title: Per-request epoch watermarking for metering safeguards
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Problem: At-least-once ingestion patterns across edge gateways and retries cause duplicate billing and quota consumption in edge→ingest→ledger flows. Intermittent network glitches and gateway restarts expose race windows where identical requests can be processed multiple times without a reliable dedupe fingerprint available. Existing ledger-based reconciliation is heavyweight and slow to converge for short-lived spikes.

Proposal summary: Introduce a compact per-request epoch watermark embedded in client requests (client_epoch + server_watermark) to give each logical request a monotonic epoch and a server-side short-lived watermark that enforces a single commit per epoch across ingestion frontends. The watermark is cheap to check, LRU-cached at the ingest layer, integrates with rate limiter quota checks, and falls back to the ledger reconciliation path for older/malformed epochs. This design aims to prevent immediate duplicates with minimal latency impact and reduce reliance on long-running reconciliation sweeps.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate requests with identical client_epoch + payload within watermark TTL are deduplicated at ingest and billed only once
End-to-end latency increase <= 2ms P50 at ingest under normal load
No user-visible 5xx increase in canary region during rollout
Fallback reconciliation still catches any missed duplicates and converges within existing SLAs
Full integration with per-customer quota counters so deduped requests do not decrement quota twice
technical_notes: Client-side: add optional epoch header X-RW-Epoch with a monotonic int per logical operation. If client cannot supply epoch, server can assign ephemeral epoch on first receive and return to client for subsequent retry attempts.

Ingress-side: maintain an in-memory LRU of (customer_id, request_fingerprint, epoch) -> commit_state with TTL (default 5m). On receive: compute fingerprint (sha256 of normalized payload + requested_model + route) and check LRU for existing committed epoch. If match and committed=true -> short-circuit accept+return previous response metadata for idempotent clients; if match and committed=false -> reject with 409 or return in-flight indicator to clients supporting polling.

Watermark semantics: server_watermark is a 64-bit monotonic token per ingest node that is stamped on acceptance and persisted to a lightweight write-ahead cache on commit. The token is not a full global sequence; it is used only to close the short race window across frontends behind the same ingress shard.

Accounting integration: billing pipeline checks commit_state before emitting consumption events. Deduped calls are annotated with dedupe_reason and attribution to original commit_id so downstream billing remains transparent in analytics dashboards.

Quota integration: quota layer consults ingest cache on decision path. If a request is deduped, quota counters are not double-decremented. For cross-node retries where cache miss occurs, quotas are checked normally and potential double-charge is later reconciled by ledger sweep.

Failure modes: cache eviction/GC may allow duplicate processing; we rely on ledger reconciliation to repair but will tune TTL to cover typical retry windows (<=5m). Clock skew between client epochs must be handled by allowing client epochs to be accepted as long as they are >= last_committed_epoch - tolerance (default 1).

Metrics & tracing: new metrics ingest.dedupe.hit, ingest.dedupe.miss, ingest.dedupe.evicted, ingest.dedupe.reconciled. Traces include epoch and fingerprint tags. Dashboards and alerting thresholds to be created in Console observability product.

Data retention & privacy: stored fingerprints are keyed by customer and have TTL; persisted commit_ids are lightweight and do not contain full payloads. All stored blobs obey customer data retention settings.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: unit/integration tests + load test harness against simulated retry storms (target date 2025-02-24)
Phase 1: Deploy ingest-side cache and epoch handling behind feature flag in canary region (us-west-2) with 5% traffic for 48h
Phase 2: Expand to 25% with live billing annotation only (no billing enforcement) and compare dedupe signal vs ledger reconciliation
Phase 3: Enable enforcement for selected low-risk customers and monitor for false positives for 7 days
Phase 4: Full rollout across regions after 2 weeks of stable canary metrics and sign-off from billing/product
Rollback plan: feature flag toggle off; triggers a reconciliation job to catch any duplicates that occurred during canary window
qa_checks: Simulate network partition: client retries across different edge gateways and verify single commit and single billing event
Replay test: send same fingerprint+epoch after TTL expiry and verify treat-as-new behavior
Concurrency test: 1000 concurrent retries of same logical request and verify at most one commit recorded
Quota test: ensure quota counters do not decrement twice in dedupe case and that rejected-in-flight flows surface correct retryable error to SDK
Chaos: restart ingest node during commit window and ensure ledger reconciliation catches any orphaned consumption events
comments: 2025-02-11 - PM review: Jordan Lee: flagged customer_impact as high; requested explicit QA scenarios for cross-region retries
2025-02-18 - Engineering note: Miguel Santos: initial prototype implemented; LRU cache library chosen is Caffeine (server-side JVM shard) and a Go shim for edge gateways
2025-02-22 - Design review: Priya Khandelwal: suggested annotated response metadata to help end-to-end tracing for customers using SDKs
2025-02-28 - Security review kickoff: Ravi Patel: flagged need for threat modeling around fingerprint inscrutability and potential replay amplification, assigned follow-up
2025-03-03 - Load test: Aisha Rahman: under sustained 95th percentile QPS, additional P50 latency of ingest path measured at +1.6ms, dedupe.hit rate 82% for scripted retry patterns
2025-03-05 - Decision: ship behind feature flag with staged rollout; billing enforced only after telemetry baseline meets thresholds
